subject: Indemnity exception request — defend-control carveout for Acme DataWorks order form
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@acmedata.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmedata.com, james.oneill@acmedata.com
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity language — defend control expectation for order form

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement has a standard requirement that our vendors accept defense control for third-party IP claims related to their service. We noticed your redline currently limits defense control and shifts to reimburse in a few scenarios.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood accept right-to-defend for third-party IP infringement tied to your product output (not customer data)?
- If not, can we get a narrow carveout that allows Acme to take control where an external claimant asserts infringement against Acme for output generated by the service?

We have a 2-week signing target. Please let me know what is possible and any evidence/SLAs you need on our side. Attaching our standard redline for reference.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Vendor Contracts | Acme DataWorks

Attachments: Acme_STANDARD_OrderForm_Redline.pdf (PDF)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Indemnity language — defend control expectation for order form

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Key points: they expect right-to-defend for IP claims tied to our output; procurement is pushing for control. They want a quick turnaround.

Quick thoughts:
- Sales: need to decide whether to offer defend (with conditions) or stick to our defend-vs-reimburse stance. Ben, can you estimate deal risk if we concede defend for this customer?
- Legal: Kimberly, need a recommended carveout we can propose (evidence obligations, cooperation, counsel approval, insurance offset, cap language).
- Marissa, ops: if we accept defend, what operational support will we need for evidence collection/timeline?

I'll coordinate once we have a proposed counter.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (PDF)]
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@acmedata.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Indemnity language — defend control expectation for order form

Hi Elaine — thanks for flagging and for the draft. Appreciate the two-week timeline; we want to move quickly too.

High-level proposal from Redwood (open to iteration):
- Redwood will grant the right to control defense for third-party IP claims that specifically allege infringement arising from model output generated for Acme (narrow scope).
- Conditions: Acme must provide prompt written notice, preserve evidence, and allow Redwood a reasonable opportunity to participate (Redwood-appointed counsel must be allowed to lead where Redwood elects).
- Redwood requests approval rights over settlement amounts that would impose ongoing obligations on Redwood or materially affect our IP.
- Financial cap: maintain the order-form cap on direct damages but allow an insurance-offset approach; Redwood proposes the existing cap of the order form (amount redacted in draft) with the option to pursue insurance proceeds first.
- Evidence & timeline: see attached evidence checklist — Acme will designate a technical liaison within 48 hours of notice and provide logs, prompts, and sample outputs within 5 business days where available.

We attached a redline with the suggested carveout (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.pdf) and an evidence checklist to speed triage. If this structure is acceptable, Kimberly will finalize the language and we can route to Procurement for a signature-ready DocuSign.

Next step: Elaine, can you confirm whether Acme's legal team needs defend unqualified (no Redwood participation) or if the conditions above are workable?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (PDF), evidence_checklist.xlsx (XLSX)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Indemnity language — defend control expectation for order form

Grace/Ben/Marissa — thanks. I reviewed Ben's proposed carveout. Legal is broadly comfortable with a narrow right-to-defend granted to Acme provided we get:

1) Narrow scope definition in the clause ("claims that arise solely from Model Output provided to Acme and not from Customer Data, custom integrations, or downstream modifications").
2) Strong notice and preservation obligations (45-day cure window for injunctive remedies, 10-day initial acknowledgment, logs within 5 business days).
3) Counsel coordination: Redwood-appointed lead counsel authorization language where Redwood elects to participate; approval rights for any settlement imposing obligations on Redwood.
4) Cap integrity: we need to preserve the economic cap in the Order Form. If Procurement insists on higher indemnity exposure, we need written approval from Revenue Leadership for an exception to the cap.

Process note: if Revenue approves a cap exception, Legal would like an insurance-offset/escrow mechanism in writing (we should avoid open-ended liability increases). Also recommend a one-time indemnity exception memo signed by the CRO and GC and attached to the PO for audit trail.

Marissa — operations: the evidence checklist looks reasonable but we need confirmation that your team can provide the requested logs within the proposed timelines. If not, we should explicitly carve out slower turnaround for archived logs.

I'll draft final redline language after we have sign-off on the cap approach.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@acmedata.com>, procurement@acmedata.com, james.oneill@acmedata.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Indemnity language — defend-control carveout and approval path (final)

Elaine / Acme team — thank you for your patience while we reviewed internally. Below is the path we can commit to today:

Summary of agreed approach (Redwood position):
- Granted: Acme may control defense for third-party IP claims that relate solely to Model Output provided by Redwood to Acme (explicitly excludes Customer Data and customer custom code).
- Conditions: prompt notice, evidence preservation, technical liaison designation within 48 hours, logs / prompts / examples provided within 5 business days where available. Redwood may appoint lead counsel to participate; any settlement that imposes obligations on Redwood requires Redwood's written consent.
- Cap / economics: Redwood will preserve the Order Form’s direct-damage cap. Procurement asked for an unlimited defense position — we cannot agree to open-ended exposure. Instead, we will accept this defend-control carveout contingent on an insurance-offset and a one-time executive exception approval for exposure above the standard cap (if Acme insists on raising the cap, that will require deal desk + CRO/GC sign-off).

Next steps:
1) Kimberly will finalize the redline and upload to the shared Drive here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Acme-MSA-redline
2) Ben will send the signature-ready order form via DocuSign after Acme confirms timing: https://app.docusign.com/ACME-042
3) Marissa will confirm technical evidence availability and turnaround; she will be Acme's ops contact for evidence triage.
4) If Acme requires a higher cap, please indicate that now so we can start the executive approval workflow (this will extend the timeline).

Elaine — can you confirm acceptance of the conditions above or indicate any absolute dealbreakers? If acceptable, we will circulate the finalized redline and DocuSign link today.

Thanks all —
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
